newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Petrol says expects listing in April.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Petrol says expects listing in April.

text.p: Slovenian petrol trading company Petrol, one of the country's five biggest firms, said on Wednesday it expected its shares to be listed on the main market of the Ljubljana bourse in April.
"We have recently applied for a listing and expect we will be listed sometime in April," Petrol's deputy executive Franci Percic told Reuters.

He said the company expected to pay a dividend of about 930 tolars this year -- its first-ever dividend -- in two instalments. The first payment of 700 tolars should be paid in April and the remainder in the last quarter of the year.
The company was privatised in December, but the state has kept a 15.63 percent stake.
Petrol, which manages 275 out of some 350 petrol stations in Slovenia, said it planned to open up to eight new stations this year.

"We expect to increase investment to some 90 million German marks this year from 44 million in 1996. The money will be spent on the construction of new stations and on the renovation of 21 old stations and a warehouse," Percic said.

Petrol said earlier its unrevised 1996 net profit fell to 2.0 billion tolars ($12.8 million) from 2.85 billion last year mainly because of low petrol prices. Slovenian petrol prices, among the lowest in Europe, are controlled by the government.
Turnover rose to 100.2 billion tolars ($0.6 billion) from 82.0 billion in 1995.
Shares of Petrol are currently being traded at between 16,500 and 20,000 tolars on the grey market. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
